{{short description|French biologist}}

[[File:Pr Barbara Demeneix.jpg|thumb|Barbara Demeinex, February 2018]]
'''Barbara Demeneix''' (born 1949) is a [[biologist]] and [[endocrinologist]]. She is currently team leader in a [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|CNRS]] research unit at the [[National Museum of Natural History (France)|National Museum of Natural History]] in Paris, France.

== Education ==
Barbara Demeneix obtained her Bachelor of Science (B.Sc. Hons) at the [[University of Wales]] and an M.Sc. at the [[University of Clermont-Ferrand]] (France). She completed her PhD in endocrinology and physiology at the [[University of Calgary]] (Canada) in 1977 as well as her Doctorat d’Etat (D.Sc.) at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University|University Paris VI]] in 1983.

== Research career ==
Between 1970 and 1981 Barbara Demeneix taught at different levels in Malawi, Canada, Morocco and France, before taking up a Lectureship at the University [[Louis Pasteur]] in Strasbourg from 1981 to 1989. During this period she undertook two research fellowships in the Molecular Neurobiology Laboratory in Cambridge (1986) and in the Max Planck Institute in Munich (1988-1989).

Since arriving at the [[National Museum of Natural History (France)|National Museum of Natural History]] in 1990 her research focused on the evolution of thyroid hormone signaling. She sought to understand how thyroid hormones activate or repress gene activity in different tissues at various developmental states and in changing physiological conditions. Working with amphibian and mouse models, she contributed to developing and optimizing techniques to study gene regulation in integrated contexts. Technologies have been patented and licensed out to SMEs (Polyplus, WatchFrog).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cnrs.fr/fr/pdf/Innovation2014_web/pubData/source/Innovation2014_web.pdf|title=CNRS, Talents du CNRS, Médaille de l'Innovation 2014|date=June 2014|website=CNRS|access-date=1 June 2017}}</ref>

In the laboratory, these methods have been applied to advance understanding of: 
* how thyroid hormone exerts negative feedback effects on hypothalamic controls, 
* how thyroid hormone regulates adult neurogenesis during aging,
* how thyroid hormone acts in early amphibian development and in metamorphosis.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://umr7221.mnhn.fr/spip.php?article96|title=UMR 7221. Team 1: Integration of transcriptional responses inducted by thyroid hormones and their receptors (Demeneix)|date=9 May 2017|access-date=6 June 2017}}</ref>
Barbara Demeneix was nominated to the Chair of Comparative Physiology in the [[National Museum of Natural History (France)|National Museum of Natural History]] in Paris in 1995.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www2.cnrs.fr/presse/communique/2370.htm|title=CNRS, Press Release "Barbara Demeneix récompensée par le magazine Nature"|date=13 December 2011|website=CNRS|access-date=1 June 2017}}</ref> This position was previously held by [[Claude Bernard]], [[Jean Pierre Flourens|Jean-Pierre Flourens]] and [[Frédéric Cuvier]]. In 1998 she took on the twin direction of Museum Comparative Physiology Laboratory and the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|CNRS]] unit UMR 7221 ‘Evolution of Endocrine Regulations’ (1998-2013). In 2001 she became director of the Department ‘Regulations and Development’ of the [[National Museum of Natural History (France)|National Museum of Natural History]], a post she held until 2017. This department grouped 3 main research units representing 200 staff.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mnhn.fr/en/node/417|title=Museum Departement 'Regulations and Development'|website=National Museum of Natural History|access-date=6 June 2017}}</ref> During this period she coordinated two large-scale European projects: CRESCENDO (2005-2011) on nuclear receptors in development and aging,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.tmpneo.com/site_crescendo/index.asp|title=CRESCENDO website|access-date=1 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190119230925/http://www.tmpneo.com/site_crescendo/index.asp|archive-date=19 January 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> and SWITCHBOX (2011-2015) on maintaining health in old age through homeostasis.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cordis.europa.eu/project/rcn/97696_en.html|title=Community Research and Development Information Service (CORDIS), SWITCHBOX project|website=European Commission|access-date=1 June 2017}}</ref>

Barbara Demeneix is active with international committees addressing thyroid hormone and endocrine disruption (including the [[Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development|OECD]]<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://www.cairn.info/revue-ecologie-et-politique-2017-1-page-135.htm|title=Barbara Demeneix, chercheuse et citoyenne|last=Deléage|first=Jean-Paul|publisher=Editions Le Bord de l’eau|year=2017|isbn=9782356875198|location=|pages=136–145}}</ref> and the European Thyroid Association<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.eurothyroid.com/about/executive_committee.html|title=ETA Executive Committee|website=European Thyroid Association|access-date=2 June 2017}}</ref>).

In 2016 she co-published an opinion column in ''[[Le Monde]]'' with more than 100 other scientists, in which they asked the [[European Union|EU]] and the international community to act against [[Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals|endocrine disrupting chemicals]]. They also condemned the use of strategies for manufacturing doubt employed by industries in the climate change battle.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.lemonde.fr/idees/article/2016/11/29/let-s-stop-the-manipulation-of-science_5039867_3232.html|title=Let's stop the manipulation of science|date=29 November 2016|work=Le Monde|access-date=1 June 2016}}</ref>

== Publications ==
Barbara Demeneix has published more than 170 scientific publications,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bdemeneix.wordpress.com/publications/|title=Barbara Demeneix's blog, Publications|date=2016-06-03|access-date=1 June 2017}}</ref> and two first-author books.

=== Books ===
* ''Losing our Minds: How environmental pollution impairs human intelligence and mental health'', [[Oxford University Press]], 2014.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Losing our minds : how environmental pollution impairs human intelligence and mental health|last=Barbara.|first=Demeneix|isbn=9780199917518|oclc=878224699|year = 2014}}</ref>   Translated into French: ''Le Cerveau endommagé: Comment la pollution altère notre intelligence et notre santé mentale'', Editions Odile Jacob, 2016.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Le Cerveau endommagé|last=Demeneix|first=Barbara|publisher=Odile Jacob|year=2016|isbn=9782738133915|location=Paris|pages=}}</ref>
* ''Toxic Cocktail: How chemical pollution is poisoning our brains'', [[Oxford University Press]], 2017.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Toxic cocktail : how chemical pollution is poisoning our brains|last=Barbara.|first=Demeneix|isbn=9780190260934|oclc=945170049|year = 2017}}</ref>   Translated into French: ''Cocktail toxique: Comment les perturbateurs endocriniens empoisonnent notre cerveau'', Editions Odile Jacob, 2017.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Cocktail toxique|last=Demeneix|first=Barbara|publisher=Odile Jacob|year=2017|isbn=978-2738140067|location=|pages=}}</ref>
